title: Weil sheaves and their representations
statement:
Use the curve $C_0$ and geometric fibre $C$ of [sk-d-real-setup]. Choose a geometric base point on $C$, and use the fibre functor of [def-galois-fibre-functor].
Let $P=\pi_1(C)$ be its profinite etale fundamental group, defined by
the fiber functor on finite etale covers. The Weil group $W(C_0)$ is the
inverse image, as in [def-wf-weil-group], of the integer powers of geometric Frobenius in
$\pi_1(C_0)\to\Gal(k/\Fq)$. It has an exact degree sequence

$$
1\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow W(C_0)
\xrightarrow{\deg}\mathbf Z\longrightarrow0.
$$

Give $W(C_0)=\pi_1(C_0)\times_{\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)}\mathbf Z$ the topology induced from $\pi_1(C_0)\times\mathbf Z$, with $\mathbf Z$ discrete; thus $P$ is open and has its profinite topology, as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Here $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is the group of invertible linear maps of $V$.

A representation $\rho:W(C_0)\to\GL(V)$ on a $\Qlb$-vector space $V$ is
lisse if its restriction to $P$ is continuous, i.e. in every basis of
$V$ the matrix coefficients of $\rho|_P$ are continuous functions on $P$
for the $\ell$-adic topology of $\Qlb$. A lisse Weil $\Qlb$-sheaf means a lisse adic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $C$ in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], together with an isomorphism $\Phi_C^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, where $\Phi_C=\operatorname{id}_{C_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(z\mapsto z^{1/q})$ and the lisse adic pullback is that of [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Its Weil fundamental representation is the stalk representation constructed there. It is
equivalently a finite-dimensional lisse representation of $W(C_0)$; for
finite-dimensional $V$ this amounts to a finite coefficient field
$E/\Ql$ and an $E$-model whose restriction to $P$ is continuous and
preserves an $\mathcal O_E$-lattice. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $\mathcal O_E$ have the meaning of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a lattice is a free $\mathcal O_E$-submodule of rank $\dim_E V_E$ spanning $V_E$. The lattice is required to be invariant under $P$; the degree-one operator need not preserve it. The quotient $\mathbf Z$ is
discrete. Choose a degree-one lift $\gamma$ and write $F=\rho(\gamma)$.
For a closed point $x$, the local Frobenius $F_x$ is the geometric
Frobenius at $x$: the image in $W(C_0)$ of the geometric Frobenius
element of a decomposition group $D_x\subset\pi_1(C_0)$ at $x$, i.e. of
the image of the geometric Frobenius of $\Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x))$
under $\pi_1(x)\to\pi_1(C_0)$ for a chosen path from a geometric point
over $x$ to the base point. It has degree $e_x$, and it is well defined
up to conjugacy in $W(C_0)$.
A constructible Weil sheaf is a globally defined adic sheaf on $C$ with an isomorphism $\Phi_C^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, whose restriction is lisse of finite rank on the geometric fibres of the strata of a finite stratification of $C_0$ into locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification]. The coefficient convention is the constructible version of the adic construction: compatible systems of constructible $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] with reduction isomorphisms, rationalized by killing uniformizer-torsion and inverting $\varpi_E$, and then the common finite-field-of-coefficients construction of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The sheaf and its Weil isomorphism are global data, not independent sheaves on the strata.

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] to the geometrically connected curve $C_0/k_0$ and its geometric fibre, obtaining the exact profinite sequence $1\to P\to G:=\pi_1(C_0)\xrightarrow r\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)\to1$. Finite fields are perfect: Frobenius is injective and therefore surjective on each finite extension. The curve is separated and of finite type and $C$ is connected by [sk-d-real-setup], so the hypotheses of the cited sequence hold. Its fibre product with $n\mapsto\gamma_k^n$, where $\gamma_k:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$, is precisely the Weil group. The second projection is surjective by surjectivity of $r$, its zero fibre is $P$, and an element mapping to $\gamma_k$ has degree one. The product topology with discrete $\mathbf Z$ makes every degree fibre open and identifies the zero fibre topologically with $P$, exactly as recorded in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. This proves the degree-sequence assertion and permits choosing $\gamma$.

Fix a basis $b$ of finite-dimensional $V$. Apply [lem-galois-aut-profinite] to the finite-etale fibre functor (a small skeleton suffices): $P$ is compact. The matrix homomorphism $g\mapsto[\rho(g)]_b$ on $P$ has continuous entries by lissity. Apply [lem-real-compact-matrix-coefficient-descent] to obtain a finite coefficient field $E_0$ containing all these entries. Enlarge $E_0$ by the finitely many entries of $F=\rho(\gamma)$ and $F^{-1}$; the resulting $E$ is still finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, since each entry is algebraic. The $E$-span $V_E$ of $b$ is stable under $P$, $F$, and $F^{-1}$. Since every $w\in W$ equals $(w\gamma^{-\deg w})\gamma^{\deg w}$ with the first factor in $P$, $V_E$ is stable under all of $W$. The restricted action is jointly continuous: its coordinates are finite sums of products of the continuous matrix entries and the coordinates of the vector, and $E$ has its subspace $\ell$-adic topology.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; proof of Proposition 1.1.12, pp. 4-5 (adjoin the degree-one matrix entries)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] to the compact group $P$ and its continuous action on $V_E$. It gives a full free $\mathcal O_E$-lattice stable under $P$, with the stated rank and adic continuity. Conversely, if such a continuous $E$-model exists, its matrix entries are continuous as $\Qlb$-valued functions in an $E$-basis. For any other $\Qlb$-basis, the new matrix is $B^{-1}A(g)B$, whose entries are finite sums of fixed scalars times entries of $A(g)$, so continuity holds in every basis. This proves the finite-model criterion without requiring $F$ to preserve the lattice.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 3; Proposition 1.1.11 and the adjoining-matrix argument pp. 4-5

proof.text: The definition of the lisse Weil pair is the one used in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]: a lisse adic sheaf with an isomorphism $\Phi_C^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, whose stalk representation extends geometric monodromy by the degree-one operator. The operator denoted $F$ is, by definition, $\rho(\gamma)$. The sentence that this stalk functor identifies lisse Weil sheaves with finite-dimensional lisse representations of $W(C_0)$ is a claim inside this definition, and it is not proved here: it is the statement of the theorem node prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence, whose statement and proof use the present definition (its degree normalization), so that node is a pointer of this definition and not a dependency (a definition does not cite a lemma about itself; citing it would close a cycle). By steps 2 and 3, the representations named there (finite-dimensional, with a finite-coefficient model continuous on $P$) are exactly the lisse representations of this statement, so the two descriptions of the representation side agree. The constructible clause is a definition: impose the same lisse finite-rank condition on a finite locally closed stratification, retaining a single global adic sheaf and a single global Weil isomorphism. It makes no assertion that a choice of sheaves on the strata alone glues.

For a closed point $x$, choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$ and a geometric point over $x$. The inclusion $x\to C_0$ induces a homomorphism on fundamental groups with the fibre-evaluation rule of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Concretely, an element of $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\kappa(x))$ acts on the fibre at $x$ of each finite etale cover by its action on the geometric points, naturally in that cover. Transport by a path to the fixed base point, using [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport], to obtain $d_x:\operatorname{Gal}(k/\kappa(x))\to G$. We check $r(d_x(\sigma))=\sigma$ in $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ on the constant covers $C_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}E$, $E\subseteq k$ finite over $k_0$, which is how [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] characterizes $r$. At the geometric point over $x$ the fibre of such a cover is $\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(E,k)$ (maps of constants, through the chosen embedding), and $\sigma$ acts by $\tau\mapsto\sigma\circ\tau$, since its action on geometric points is precomposition with $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. The path restricted to constant covers is a natural isomorphism between two fibre functors of the finite etale covers of $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, both identified with $E\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(E,k)$. Apply [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] to $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ (separated, finite type, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ connected): its geometric group $\operatorname{Aut}$ of the fibre functor of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is trivial, because finite etale $k$-schemes are finite disjoint unions of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and a natural automorphism of the fibre functor on these is the identity; hence every automorphism of that fibre functor is $\tau\mapsto u\circ\tau$ for a unique $u\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. So transport along the path conjugates the action $\tau\mapsto\sigma\circ\tau$ by such a $u$. Since $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)\cong\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ is abelian [det-base-field-cd-galois-group], $u\sigma u^{-1}=\sigma$, and the characterization of $r$ gives $r(d_x(\sigma))=\sigma$. Define $F_x=d_x(\gamma_x)$, with $\gamma_x:z\mapsto z^{1/q^{e_x}}$. Since $\gamma_x=\gamma_k^{e_x}$, it lies in $W$ and has degree $e_x$.

source.place: (1.1.8), p. 151, and (1.1.13), p. 152 (residue Galois map and its projection on constants)

proof.text: If the path is changed, [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport] says that $F_x$ changes to $gF_xg^{-1}$ for some $g\in G$. This includes changing the residue embedding: choose an isomorphism of the two algebraic closures over $\kappa(x)$ and compose the paths; geometric Frobenius is unchanged under that isomorphism, since it is the inverse of the $q^{e_x}$-power map. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], the restriction of $r(g)$ to $\kappa(x)$ is $\gamma_k^n|_{\kappa(x)}$ for an integer $n$, because inverse Frobenius generates the same finite cyclic Galois group. Put $\sigma=\gamma_k^{-n}r(g)$; it fixes $\kappa(x)$ and thus belongs to $\operatorname{Gal}(k/\kappa(x))$. This group is abelian by [det-base-field-cd-galois-group]. Therefore $a=d_x(\sigma)$ commutes with $F_x=d_x(\gamma_x)$. As $r(a)=\sigma$, the element $w=ga^{-1}$ satisfies $r(w)=r(g)\sigma^{-1}=\gamma_k^n$, so $w\in W$. Finally $wF_xw^{-1}=ga^{-1}F_xag^{-1}=gF_xg^{-1}$. Hence every change is already conjugation inside $W$, as claimed.

source.place: (1.1.13), pp. 152-153: the residue Galois image centralizes F_x and projects onto the open constant-field subgroup
